correctness.rationale: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.21286v1 supplies a Borel random independent set containing each vertex with the fixed probability \(p=2^{-d-1}\). The new list hypothesis guarantees at least \(d+1\) available permitted colors after deleting all out-neighbor colors. Recoloring a selected sad vertex to one of these \(d+1\) choices is Borel, keeps the color in its list, and makes that vertex happy because the selected set is independent. For each vertex, the same union bound as in the source gives \(\mathbb P(S_{n+1}(x))\le\alpha^n((1-p)+d_G^+(x)p/(d+1))\le\alpha^{n+1}\), where \(\alpha=1-p/(d+1)<1\). Borel--Cantelli yields eventual stabilization, and finite out-degree then gives edgewise almost-sure propriety of the Borel limit. The Borel selection from varying lists is justified by finite-section projection and the natural order on \(\mathbb N\). No experiment or partial enumeration substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: List colorability is a standard robustness strengthening of ordinary coloring, and the statement is not merely the uniform \((2d+1)\)-list analogue: it gives the local threshold \(d+d_G^+(x)+1\), strictly reducing the required list size at vertices below the global out-degree maximum. It retains the sharp universal constant \(2d+1\), with regular tournaments providing the obstruction to any uniform improvement. This is a natural extension of a new sharp descriptive-coloring theorem and is directly reusable when admissible colors vary by vertex.
